harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/legacy2/numeric-record-ordering/bin/merge on node1. It now performs CSV-aware numeric ordering, emits one header, collapses identical duplicates, rejects conflicting duplicates without replacing merged.csv, and persists across reboot on the unchanged CentOS 5.11 / 2.6.18 platform.
actions_performed: Implemented a Python 2.4-compatible CSV merge using same-directory temporary output and atomic publication.
Verified the result contains IDs 2, 10, 100 in numeric order and preserves the quoted field "Tape, wide".
Verified conflicting transaction ID 2 exits with an explanatory error while the published file's checksum and inode remain unchanged.
Safely restarted node1 and repeated functional and conflict-preservation checks after recovery.

evidence.requirement: Numeric ordering, quoted comma retention, one header, and identical duplicate collapse
evidence.summary: Independent CSV validation showed one header and exactly IDs 2,10,100; "Tape, wide" remained one field and duplicate ID 2 appeared once.

evidence.requirement: Conflicting duplicates stop publication and explain the conflict
evidence.summary: Conflict tests exited 1, identified both conflicting ID 2 records, and proved the output checksum and inode remained unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Retain the installed legacy operating system and kernel
evidence.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 were unchanged; implementation uses the installed Python 2.4.3 runtime.

Healthy baseline boot ID 0567cf33-f178-48ce-8000-000000000000 was captured, reboot acknowledged, disconnection observed, and recovery proved with changed boot ID 0212ffb2-4333-4d15-8000-000000000000, running SSH, intact checksums, and successful post-restart merge and conflict tests.
